_comment: M0 managed settings: OBSERVATION ONLY. Deliver via MDM to
/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/managed-settings.json (macOS) or
/etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json (Linux and WSL),
C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json (Windows; the legacy
C:\ProgramData location is not read), or via server-managed settings on
claude.ai.
This file deliberately contains NO permission changes and NO sandbox
enablement. Its one sandbox entry, 127.0.0.1 in network.allowedDomains, lets
ambitd's http hooks through the sandbox proxy on a machine that runs Claude
Code with the sandbox on (docs/06, blocker 7); it does not turn the sandbox on.
M0's exit criterion is zero developer-visible behavior change apart from that
entry, because a baseline cannot be measured from a system that is already
changing behavior. Enforcement keys are not part of this file and are not
deployed until the promotion ladder (shadow, then ask, then deny; see the
Roadmap in README.md) has evidence behind it.
Managed settings sit at the highest precedence: no other level, including
command-line arguments, overrides a managed permission rule, and managed
hooks cannot be disabled by user or project settings. That is what makes
this file the anchor, and why SCA policy ambit_managed_settings asserts it
is still here and still correct (detector D12).

_comment_protocol: http/json, NOT grpc or http/protobuf. ambitd's receiver decodes OTLP/JSON
with the standard library; the alternatives would pull grpc and protobuf
runtimes into a daemon that ships to developer endpoints and currently has
zero dependencies, which is a large supply-chain surface to add to a
Port 4318, NOT 4317. 4318 is the OTLP/HTTP default; 4317 is gRPC. An
earlier version of this file had 4317 with HTTP intent, which would have
exported into a dead port: Claude Code would look configured while nothing
was ever received. ambitd answers 415 on a protobuf body and reports
degraded health rather than failing silently, precisely because that blind
spot is what the second stream exists to close.
_comment_content_gates: are deliberately NOT set in M0. They are off by default, and turning them
on ships tool arguments, file contents and full conversation history into
the OTLP stream. ambitd already gets what it needs from the hook payloads;
enabling these would widen the sensitive-data surface for no M0 benefit.

_comment: Every event below is observation only. PreToolUse is included because it
is the only event carrying tool_input before execution, and ambitd returns
an empty response to it: no decision, so Claude Code's permission
pipeline behaves exactly as it would with no hook installed.
An empty response is NOT the same as returning allow. Returning allow
would suppress the permission prompt a developer would otherwise see.
SessionStart is the one event registered as a command, not http. Claude
Code v2.1.278 fires it but does not deliver it to an http hook (observed on
Windows: the same event reached a command hook and never an http one).
`ambitd hook-forward` reads the payload on stdin, posts it unchanged to
ambitd, prints nothing (a SessionStart hook's stdout becomes model
context) and always exits 0. The binary is named by absolute path, where
the system installer puts it, because a managed hook must not depend on
whose PATH Claude Code was started with. There is one bundle per OS family
for that reason; they differ only in that command.
